root_cause.text: The v3d_perfmon_find() function increments the reference count of performance monitor objects, but callers in v3d_perfmon_set_global_ioctl() and v3d_perfmon_delete() failed to decrement these references on error paths and when clearing or destroying global performance monitors, leading to reference count leaks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix reference counting leak by conditionally releasing the global perfmon reference only when it is successfully cleared from the global pointer.
intent_record.what: Modified the global perfmon cleanup logic: wrapped the cmpxchg() call in an if-condition to check if it successfully replaced the perfmon, and added a conditional v3d_perfmon_put(perfmon) call inside the if-block. Updated the comment to explain reference counting semantics.
intent_record.how: The original code unconditionally attempted to clear the global perfmon pointer but did not release the reference that was acquired when the perfmon was set as global. The new code only calls v3d_perfmon_put() on the global reference if cmpxchg() confirms the swap succeeded (i.e., the perfmon was actually the active global perfmon). This ensures proper reference counting: one put for the global reference (conditional) and one put for the local reference (unconditional at the end).

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix reference counting leaks in v3d_perfmon_set_global_ioctl by properly releasing perfmon objects in all code paths.
intent_record.what: Added explicit reference counting for perfmon objects in v3d_perfmon_set_global_ioctl: (1) introduced `old` variable to capture the swapped-out perfmon pointer, (2) added v3d_perfmon_put(perfmon) call before clearing global_perfmon, (3) added v3d_perfmon_put(old) after xchg to release the old reference, (4) added v3d_perfmon_put(perfmon) in the cmpxchg failure path, (5) added explanatory comment about reference handling, and (6) reformatted the cmpxchg condition with braces.
intent_record.how: This change ensures proper reference counting cleanup for perfmon objects. Previously, when clearing the global perfmon or when setting fails due to an existing perfmon, the perfmon references were not being released, causing potential memory leaks. Now: (a) when clearing, the old perfmon is properly released via v3d_perfmon_put(old), (b) when the set operation fails because a perfmon already exists, the input perfmon is released via v3d_perfmon_put(perfmon), and (c) the input perfmon is released before clearing to avoid holding unnecessary references.

candidates.rationale: This line clears the global perfmon pointer without releasing the reference count of the perfmon object that was previously stored there. The xchg() operation discards the old pointer value without calling v3d_perfmon_put() to decrement its reference count, causing a leak.

This check validates the global_perfmon exists before clearing it, but the subsequent xchg() at line 467 fails to release the reference of the perfmon being cleared, indicating the error path doesn't properly handle reference counting.

When cmpxchg() fails (global_perfmon is not NULL), the function returns -EBUSY without releasing the reference count of the perfmon object that was incremented by v3d_perfmon_find(). This is an error path reference leak.

This cmpxchg() may fail to clear the global_perfmon if it was already changed by another thread, but the code unconditionally calls v3d_perfmon_put() afterward regardless of whether the cmpxchg succeeded, potentially releasing a reference that wasn't actually removed from the global pointer.

    drm/v3d: Add DRM_IOCTL_V3D_PERFMON_SET_GLOBAL
    
    Add a new ioctl, DRM_IOCTL_V3D_PERFMON_SET_GLOBAL, to allow
    configuration of a global performance monitor (perfmon).
    Use the global perfmon for all jobs to ensure consistent
    performance tracking across submissions. This feature is
    needed to implement a Perfetto datasources in user-space.
bic_trace_step.reason: The new v3d_perfmon_set_global_ioctl() function calls v3d_perfmon_find() at line 478, which increments the reference count of the perfmon object. However, there are multiple error paths where the reference count is not decremented: (1) Line 480-481: if perfmon is NULL, the function returns -EINVAL without decrementing; (2) Line 483-485: if CLEAR_GLOBAL flag is set and global_perfmon is NULL, returns -EINVAL without decrementing the reference that was just incremented; (3) Line 490: if cmpxchg fails (global_perfmon is not NULL), returns -EBUSY without decrementing the reference. Additionally, line 488 shows xchg() being called to clear the global perfmon, but there's no corresponding v3d_perfmon_put() call to decrement the reference of the old perfmon being replaced. The function increments a reference count via v3d_perfmon_find() but fails to properly manage that reference on error paths and when replacing/clearing the global perfmon.

bic_trace_step.reason: The code shows the vulnerable construct clearly. In v3d_perfmon_find() (lines 81-89), the function calls v3d_perfmon_get(perfmon) at line 86, which increments the reference count via refcount_inc(). However, examining the callers in this commit: (1) v3d_perfmon_get_values_ioctl() calls v3d_perfmon_find() indirectly via idr_find() and v3d_perfmon_get() at lines 197-198, then calls v3d_perfmon_put() at line 209 - this one is handled correctly. (2) The vulnerability description mentions v3d_perfmon_set_global_ioctl() and v3d_perfmon_delete() as problematic callers, but these functions are NOT present in this commit's diff. The diff only shows the initial introduction of the perfmon infrastructure. Looking at v3d_perfmon_get_values_ioctl() more carefully: it calls v3d_perfmon_get(perfmon) at line 198 after idr_find(), then properly decrements with v3d_perfmon_put() at line 209. However, there is a missing v3d_perfmon_put() on the error path at line 201 when perfmon is NULL - the function returns -EINVAL without decrementing the reference that was incremented at line 198 (though in this case perfmon is NULL so get() was a no-op). The real bug is that v3d_perfmon_find() itself increments the refcount (line 86) and returns the perfmon, making it the caller's responsibility to decrement. This is a reference count leak pattern where callers must remember to call v3d_perfmon_put(), but the code structure makes this error-prone. The vulnerable construct IS PRESENT: v3d_perfmon_find() increments refcount without the caller having clear ownership semantics, and there's no fix in place to prevent leaks.
